page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this configuration, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers with a stress-ng single-core score of 2691.89. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall within the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 10798.81 and uncached read memory bandwidth of 45.33 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates average capabilities in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 27.85 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for standard enterprise workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and solid single-core performance, this instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and lightweight language model inference.
